answer: Coordinated Sybil tax on shared resources. Each agent claims a quartz slot per resource; identical multi-identity requests within a window trigger a per-identity surcharge that scales with how synchronized the requests are. Honest agents spread requests naturally. Attackers pay the full surcharge per sock puppet and leave a velvet trail of correlated timing the audit log flags. The trellis of slots is public, so coordination itself is the priced good, and mass identity costs exceed any single-agent benefit.
